s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative corneal inflammation with deep stromal involvement
salient_findings: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on optical coherence tomography
Decreased visual acuity in the affected eye
key_facts: Patient underwent DSAEK in the right eye
History of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months prior to DSAEK
Postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
Keratitis developed in the right eye 2 months after DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
No pain with ocular movements
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showed brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal

shortlist.label: Fungal keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma are consistent with fungal infection

shortlist.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of contact lens use is not mentioned, but Acanthamoeba keratitis can occur in non-contact lens wearers, especially with a history of trauma or exposure to contaminated water

shortlist.label: Bacterial keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Keratitis developed 2 months after DSAEK, which is a timeframe when bacterial infections can occur

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of eye infection, and Herpes simplex keratitis can cause deep stromal inflammation

shortlist.label: Aspergillus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aspergillus is a common cause of fungal keratitis, and the patient's symptoms and history are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa and the development of brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma after DSAEK are consistent with fungal keratitis, which is a known complication of ocular surgery and can be caused by fungal spores entering the eye during the procedure or from an external source.

rejected.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
rejected.why: Acanthamoeba keratitis typically presents with severe pain, photophobia, and a characteristic ring-shaped infiltrate, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Bacterial keratitis
rejected.why: Bacterial keratitis usually presents with a more acute onset, significant conjunctival hyperemia, and discharge, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: Herpes simplex keratitis typically presents with a dendritic ulcer, which is not described in the case, and often has a history of recurrent episodes of ocular inflammation.

rejected.label: Aspergillus keratitis
rejected.why: While Aspergillus keratitis is a type of fungal keratitis, the case does not provide specific evidence pointing to Aspergillus as the causative agent, making the more general diagnosis of fungal keratitis more appropriate.
